questions.prompt: What is a stock?
choices: A tiny piece of a company
A loan you give to a bank
questions.explanation: When you buy a stock (or share), you own a tiny piece of that company.

questions.prompt: Stock prices can go up AND down.
questions.explanation: True! Prices change every day. That's why investing is for the long term.

questions.prompt: If you own a share of Byte Burger, you are a…
questions.explanation: Shareholders own part of the company.

questions.prompt: Why might a company's stock price go UP?
choices: It is selling lots and earning more
It rained in Fin City yesterday
The company lost lots of customers
Its new logo is a brighter blue
questions.explanation: When a company does well and earns more, people want to own it, so the price goes up.

questions.prompt: What does 'don't put all your eggs in one basket' mean for investing?
choices: Own many companies, not just one
Buy eggs whenever they are cheap
Only ever buy one single stock
Keep your money in a real basket
questions.explanation: If one company has a bad year, owning others helps. That's diversification!

questions.prompt: One share costs ${p}. How much do {n} shares cost?
questions.explanation: ${p} × {n} = ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: You bought a share for ${b}. Now it's worth ${s}. How much did you gain?
questions.explanation: ${s} − ${b} = ${ANSWER} gain.

questions.prompt: An index fund is like…
choices: A basket of tiny pieces of many companies
One single company you know well
A piggy bank with a lock
questions.explanation: An index fund owns a little of lots of companies, so it's diversified automatically.

questions.prompt: Which is usually the SAFEST?
choices: A hot stock everyone's talking about
A coin someone says will go 'to the moon'
questions.explanation: Savings accounts are very safe (but grow slowly). New companies and hype are risky.

questions.prompt: Some companies share part of their profit with shareholders. That payment is called a…
questions.explanation: A dividend is money a company pays to its shareholders.

questions.prompt: Risk and reward usually go together. That means…
choices: What can grow more can also drop more
Safe things always grow the fastest
Risky things can never lose money
A big reward means there is no risk
questions.explanation: Investments with bigger possible gains usually have bigger possible losses too.

questions.prompt: A friend says 'Buy this coin, it will make you rich by Friday!' What should you think?
questions.explanation: Promises of getting rich super fast are a warning sign.

questions.prompt: You own {n} shares. Each pays a ${d} dividend. How much do you get?
questions.explanation: {n} × ${d} = ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: A stock dropped a little this week. A long-term investor usually…
choices: Moves it all into a new hot stock
questions.explanation: Prices go up and down. Long-term investors don't panic over short dips.

questions.prompt: You invest ${p}. It grows 10% this year. How much do you have now?
questions.explanation: 10% of ${p} is added: ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: A bond is…
choices: An IOU: you lend money and earn interest
A small piece of a company you own
A credit card you use to buy shares
A rare coin that collectors trade
questions.explanation: When you buy a bond, you lend money to a company or government, and they pay you back with interest.

questions.prompt: Investing a little bit every month is a good idea because…
choices: Money has more time to grow
Prices never change from month to month
You are only allowed to invest once
It costs more than investing once a year
questions.explanation: Investing regularly builds the habit and smooths out ups and downs.

questions.prompt: A 'market' is a place where…
choices: People go to sleep at night
questions.explanation: Markets are where buyers and sellers trade. The stock market trades shares of companies.

questions.prompt: When LOTS of people want to buy a stock, its price usually…
questions.explanation: More buyers than sellers pushes the price up.

questions.prompt: Prices slowly going up over time is called…
questions.explanation: Inflation means things cost a little more each year.

questions.prompt: If prices go up 3% a year but your money in a jar grows 0%, what happens?
choices: Your money buys less over time
Your money buys more over time
questions.explanation: Money that doesn't grow loses buying power to inflation.

questions.prompt: A 'bull market' means prices are mostly…
questions.explanation: Bulls charge forward (up!). Bears swipe down, a bear market means prices are falling.

questions.prompt: A 'bear market' means prices are mostly…
questions.explanation: Bear markets are when prices fall for a while.

questions.prompt: Money that grows on top of your earlier growth is called…
questions.explanation: Compound growth is like a snowball getting bigger as it rolls.

questions.prompt: $100 grows 10% the first year and 10% again the second year. How much after 2 years?
questions.explanation: Year 1: $100 → $110. Year 2: $110 + $11 = $121. The extra $1 is compound growth!

questions.prompt: If a company goes out of business, its stock can become worth…
questions.explanation: Stocks can lose all their value. That's why we spread money across many companies.

questions.prompt: Which news would make a toy store’s stock go up?
choices: The biggest store had to close
A whole shipment of toys broke
questions.explanation: Strong sales mean more profit, which is good for the stock.

questions.prompt: A share was ${a} and dropped to ${b}. How much did it lose?
questions.explanation: ${a} − ${b} = ${ANSWER} loss.

questions.prompt: You lost money on a stock but didn't sell. Is the loss 'locked in'?
choices: Not yet, the price could come back
Yes, the loss is locked in forever
The bank keeps the money it lost
questions.explanation: A loss isn't final until you sell. That's why patient investors don't panic-sell.

questions.prompt: Someone says 'Give me $10 and I promise to give you $100 tomorrow!' This is probably…
questions.explanation: Promises that sound too good to be true usually are.

questions.prompt: Which job helps people buy and sell stocks?
questions.explanation: Stockbrokers (and brokerage apps) help people trade investments.

questions.prompt: Why do people invest instead of keeping all their money in a piggy bank?
choices: Piggy banks are against the law
Because they want to lose it
Investing has no risk at all
questions.explanation: Investing gives money a chance to grow faster than prices rise, though it can go down too.

questions.prompt: You split $20 equally between 4 companies. How much in each?
questions.explanation: $20 ÷ 4 = $5 each, diversified!

questions.prompt: The chart line goes up, up, up over many months. This is called an…
questions.explanation: A trend is the general direction over time.

questions.prompt: Green on a stock chart usually means the price went…
questions.explanation: Green usually means up, red means down.

questions.prompt: A brand-new company with a cool idea is called a…
questions.explanation: Startups are new businesses. Some grow huge, many fail.

questions.prompt: Most new startups succeed and make their investors rich.
questions.explanation: False, most startups fail. A few big winners are why people still invest in them.

questions.prompt: News says 'People are buying lots of pets!' Which company might do well?
questions.explanation: More pets → more pet food sales!

questions.prompt: A big storm closed the harbor. Which company is MOST hurt?
questions.explanation: Ships can't move cargo, so shipping companies lose money.

questions.prompt: Which plan is the smartest for a young investor?
choices: A little each month in a fund, and patience
Everything in one hot stock right now
Buying and selling every single day
Waiting until you are rich to start saving
questions.explanation: Regular investing, diversification and patience are the winning recipe.

questions.prompt: You have ${m}. A share costs ${p}. How many whole shares can you buy?
questions.explanation: ${m} ÷ ${p} = {ANSWER:int} shares.

questions.prompt: New York's Stock Exchange is a place where people…
choices: Buy and sell shares of companies
questions.explanation: Stock exchanges are markets for company shares.

questions.prompt: Who ends up with more money: someone who starts investing at 15 or at 35 (same amount each month)?
questions.explanation: Starting early gives compound growth more years to work.

questions.prompt: Your $50 investment grew to $75. How much did it grow?
An index fund owns pieces of many companies at once.
questions.explanation: True! That's what makes it diversified.

questions.prompt: News: 'Fin City Reserve makes borrowing more expensive.' What happens to loan interest rates?
questions.explanation: When the central bank raises rates, loans cost more.

questions.prompt: Which is an example of investing?
choices: Losing your wallet at the park
questions.explanation: Investing means buying something you hope will grow in value.

questions.prompt: You invest $10 every month for one year. How much did you invest in total?
A celebrity online says a stock will 'definitely triple.' What's wise?
choices: Buy as many shares as you can right away
Borrow money so you can buy even more
Tell all of your friends to buy it too
questions.explanation: No one can promise the future. Hype often ends badly.

questions.prompt: A company's share price is $2 and another's is $200. Which company is 'better'?
choices: You can’t tell from the price
They are both exactly the same
questions.explanation: Share price alone doesn't tell you if a company is good. You have to look at how the business is doing.

questions.prompt: Who decides the price of a stock each day?
questions.explanation: Prices move as buyers and sellers agree on trades.

questions.prompt: Owning both a burger company and a shoe company is safer than owning just one because…
choices: If one has a bad year, the other may be fine
They are secretly the same company
Two companies are guaranteed to go up
questions.explanation: Different companies often have good and bad years at different times.
